question: Is the retained same-forest execution advantage repeatable in a bounded repeated-process supplement on this shared machine?
scope: Execution only. Preserve the original six scenario/root conditions and search semantics. No playing-strength, compiler, build, cross-machine or cross-platform evaluation.
order: For block b and iteration i, rotate the six condition indices by b+i. For original condition index c, use original ORDERS[(b+i+c)%6]. Across six blocks every phase occupies every position four times per condition. Two iterations within one fresh controller are nested observations, not independent processes.
sampling_levels: One source/interpreter installation and build. Six fresh Python controller invocations are the outer sampling units. Two full triplets per condition are inner repetitions. Every execution constructs fresh trees; each process execution constructs a fresh pool. There are three fixed initial states and one fixed search seed, not a sampled workload distribution.
timing: Reuse original elapsed_s: sequential/cold include engine construction and search, warm excludes separately recorded fresh-pool preparation. Add complete_call_s around the existing execute helper, including preparation, search, receipt conversion, root-mutation check and owned pool close. Controller invocation wall time is separate and not apportioned among modes. Do not sum overlapping components or call a residual pure cleanup/IPC time.
analysis: For each condition, phase and timing metric, average the two paired log(sequential/process) ratios within each fresh controller block. Give the exponentiated mean of those six block means and an approximate 95-percent Student-t interval using six sampling units, df=5 and critical value 2.571. This is a geometric mean paired ratio, not the ratio of arithmetic means. Retain all 12 raw ratios and both nested variance components. Intervals assume reasonably independent approximately normal process-block means. Shared activity, drift and six blocks limit that assumption. These are individual descriptive intervals without simultaneous familywise coverage.
deciding_result: Only complete, source-stable, exactly matching work receives timing analysis. For each predeclared interval, lower>1 supports a bounded execution advantage. Upper<1 supports a bounded disadvantage. An interval containing 1 is inconclusive. No global speedup or playing-strength claim follows. Complete-call results qualify any warm-search advantage.
resource_policy: At most four owned process workers, one controller at a time. Require an externally owned whole-process-tree wall/memory bound for collection. Pause competing owned benchmarks, browser checks, compilers and renderers. Preserve ordinary user applications and settings. The 300-second soft collection deadline reserves 70 seconds before each new call. The external process-tree bound handles a stuck call or cleanup. No exclusive-machine claim.
failure_policy: Create a new attempt directory exclusively. Write every running cell before executing it, then its outcome. Preserve partial blocks, logs, nonzero exits, interrupted source checks and all unfavorable timings. Stop after first execution/receipt/root/source mismatch or maximum-cost admission refusal. Do not replace/retry that attempt. An incomplete attempt has no six-block confidence interval.
source_identity: Commit and independently review the runner and protocol before measurement. Require a clean worktree. Record revision, normalized LF source hashes, interpreter executable/version/platform and original retained result identity; verify source again after each block and at the end.
method_basis: Kalibera and Jones (2013), DOI 10.1145/2464157.2464160: inspected fetched abstract, author webpage and repository abstract only. Corrected full manuscript retrieval timed out. Use its separation of repetition levels as method context, not a claim to implement its full cost/Fieller model. NIST Handbook 1.3.5.2 and 1.3.6.7.2 provide the declared ordinary Student-t mean interval and rounded df 5 critical value. No outcomes have been measured under this protocol at declaration.
